checkpoint_metadata.runtime_scope: No historic training runtime descriptor in this checkpoint; only recorded device and precision are known here. No present-day runtime or source defaults substituted.

interpretation.claim_boundary: Finite-precision F is neither a certified lower bound nor a proof. These selected candidates do not establish optimality, impossibility, or a dimension lower bound; the original mathematical goals remain open.
interpretation.current_result: A reusable numerical candidate with stored full-word CPU measurements; nonzero leakage and target residual remain.
interpretation.data_status: Source experimental data, not a ledger entry, freeze output, or formal certificate.
interpretation.physical_status: The stored float32 arrays have floating Gram error and output norm different from one. They are approximate isometries, not exactly physical certified witnesses.

model.ideal_constraints: sum_label A[label].T @ A[label] = I_D and v0.T @ v0 = 1. The same real V is repeated eight times; initial memory is pure and final memory is traced.
model.metric_meaning: t=sum_legal psi_w/sqrt(840); stored target_fidelity F=||t||^2 is the raw target projection weight, with no division by output norm_squared. The target-separated-memory residual measures ||Psi - target tensor t||; forbidden leakage sums ||psi_w||^2 over illegal words.

restrictions.interpretation: finite precision evidence, not success, closure, or a lower bound
restrictions.isometry: one fixed V: R^D -> R^4 tensor R^D, used eight times

model.target: Pure state with amplitude +1/sqrt(840) on each of the 840 length-8 words of occupation (4,2,1,1), and zero on every other word.
model.tensor_order: A[label,next_memory,memory]; V row = label*D + next_memory. Word w=(w0,...,w7) has final-memory vector psi_w=A[w7]...A[w0]v0.

reproduction.arguments: Replace REPOSITORY_ROOT with an explicit path to the repository and RESULT_JSON with an explicit path to this file; quote paths containing spaces. Invocation is independent of the working directory.
reproduction.command:
python3 -B - REPOSITORY_ROOT RESULT_JSON <<'PYTHON'
import json, sys
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import torch
repo, result_file = map(Path, sys.argv[1:])
sys.path.insert(0, str(repo / "tools/scripts/agent/gpu5040"))
from state_store import tensor_digest
from tensor_core import verify_full_output
r = json.loads(result_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
x = r["tensors"]
assert x["dtype"] == "float32"
a = np.asarray(x["matrices"], dtype=np.float32)
v = np.asarray(x["initial"], dtype=np.float32)
assert list(a.shape) == x["matrices_shape"]
assert list(v.shape) == x["initial_shape"]
assert sys.byteorder == x["digest_byte_order"]
assert tensor_digest(torch.from_numpy(a), torch.from_numpy(v)) == r["candidate_sha256"]
measured = verify_full_output(a, v, occupation=tuple(r["model"]["occupation"]),
                              chunk_size=r["verification"]["result"]["chunk_size"])
print(json.dumps(measured, indent=2, allow_nan=False))
PYTHON
reproduction.comparison: Compare measured scientific fields with verification.result. Seconds is runtime-dependent; floating reductions can differ across NumPy/BLAS/platform versions. Historical UTC/runtime metadata are not regenerated by verify_full_output.
reproduction.dependencies: Python 3 with NumPy and PyTorch on CPU; little-endian for the recorded tensor_digest. Known verification runtime versions, when available, are in verification.result.verification_runtime.
reproduction.precision: Decode numeric arrays as float32 exactly. Existing verify_full_output then promotes the unchanged float32 values to NumPy float64 for its two enumeration passes; this is evaluation arithmetic, not a replacement candidate.
reproduction.purpose: Reevaluate these saved arrays only; no training or checkpoint is needed.

tensors.encoding: JSON numeric arrays contain exact stored binary32 values; no rounding, refit, QR, normalization, or precision substitution.
